Safety · Read First

Hazardous Voltage — Qualified Personnel Only

  • This equipment operates at lethal three-phase voltages and high currents. Installation, inspection and repair must be performed only by qualified electrical personnel.
  • Before opening the cabinet or touching any internal part: switch OFF the AVR and the upstream supply, isolate and lock-out / tag-out, then verify with a meter that all terminals are de-energised.
  • Wait for capacitors and the switching power supply to discharge before handling the PCB. Treat every conductor as live until proven otherwise.
  • Use insulated tools and proper PPE. Never work alone on energised or partially energised equipment. Do not bypass interlocks except as described for the maintenance bypass procedure.
  • After any repair, restore all guards, earth connections and insulation before re-energising. Re-check phase sequence and input voltage against the nameplate.
  • If you are unsure, stop and contact service. Incorrect wiring or settings can cause electric shock, fire, or damage to the load.
01
Chapter One

Product Basics & Precautions for Use

1-1

Quick Checks Before Disassembly / Calling Service

Many “faults” are not hardware failures. Run through this list before opening the cabinet or contacting service — it often saves a site visit.

  1. No output? Check the start / bypass switch position (see 1-4). In bypass the load is fed directly; in start the AVR regulates. Confirm the correct breaker is ON.
  2. Measure the input voltage on all phases. If it is outside the unit's nameplate regulating range, the AVR cannot correct it — this is normal operation, not a fault. Correct the supply or consult service about the range.
  3. Output too high / too low but stable? Check the P02 output set value (2-3) and the P01 accuracy setting (2-2).
  4. Trips / overload? Check the load current against the rating and the P03 protection setting (2-4). Reduce the load or correct P03 if mis-set.
  5. Listen / look: is the cooling fan running and the cabinet ventilated? Overheating can cause unstable output. See 3-7.
  6. Visual check without disassembly: loose terminal lugs, burnt smell, tripped external protection, or an abnormal LCD indication — note any fault / exception shown and report it to service.
  7. Still faulty? Note the model, serial number, the exact symptom and any LCD indication, then contact service (see footer). Do not open the cabinet unless qualified (see Safety above).
1-2

Product Introduction & Main Accessories

The AVR series is a servo-motor-driven automatic voltage regulator for industrial three-phase loads. The front panel hosts the LCD control unit and membrane keys; the rear carries the input/output terminals and the manual bypass switch.

Main internal components — the cabinet integrates the control board, drive power supply, surge protection, current sensing and the regulating/compensation magnetics:

  • PCB control main board (Model 2026)
  • Main-board switching power supply
  • SPD — surge protective device
  • L1 / L2 / L3 main current transformers
  • Center (isolation compensation) transformer
  • L1 / L2 / L3 voltage-regulating coils
  • Output protection contactor
  • Servo motors & conductive carbon brushes
1-3

Precautions for Installing the Power Supply

CautionVerify that the input power supply is correct before booting — confirm phase sequence, voltage level and earthing against the unit nameplate. Energising with wrong input can damage the regulator or the load.
1-4

AVR Start & Bypass Switch Operation

ModeProcedure
Normal startCheck that the input power supply is correct, then close the AVR circuit breaker directly.
BypassTurn off the AVR start switch, move the circuit-breaker interlock mechanism, then close the bypass switch.

03
Chapter Three

Maintenance & Component Replacement

3-1

Mainboard & Display Screen Replacement

When the control main board or LCD is damaged, replace it with a board of the same specification. The key point is to ensure every connecting wire is re-seated correctly, with no mistakes.

CompatibilityCheck that the silkscreen code on the PCB is identical — boards with the same code are interchangeable. Example codes: P31-33.8 XKR (AC 3P, three-phase three-wire) and P31-35.5A XKR (AC 3P+N, three-phase four-wire).
3-2

Servo Motor Replacement

  1. Loosen the fixing-bracket screw and lift the servo motor out from the top of the coil.
  2. Remove the three screws securing the motor to its mounting flange.
  3. Re-solder / reconnect the positive & negative drive wires to the new motor.
3-3

Conductive Carbon Brush Replacement

  1. Loosen the fixing-bracket screw and remove the carbon-brush holder from the top.
  2. Disconnect the conductive wires, then install the new carbon-brush module and re-tighten.
3-4

Mainboard Power Supply Check

  1. Check the switching-PSU input AC 135 V (normal range AC 130–150 V).
  2. If input is normal, measure the DC 12 V output. No output ⇒ PSU is faulty.
  3. Replace with a matching DC 12 V supply to power the main board.
3-5

Voltage Regulating Coil Replacement

  1. Replace with the same specification coil — solder joints at 0 V / 135 V / 220 V.
  2. Disconnect the carbon brushes and the servo motor before removing the coil.
  3. Mind the servo insulating base — it has three screws.
  4. Both the lower insulating base and the upper insulating barrel carry insulating gaskets — refit them correctly.
CautionUsing a coil of the wrong specification can cause unstable output voltage or equipment damage.
3-6

Isolation Compensation Transformer Replacement

WarningPay close attention to the power-cord wiring — incorrect connection causes unstable output voltage. Double-check every lead before energising.
3-7

Cooling Fan Replacement

  1. If the fan does not run, first verify the 220 V fan supply is present.
  2. If voltage is normal but the fan is still dead, the fan is faulty — replace it directly.
3-8

Current Transformer Replacement

  1. A faulty CT makes the operating current read 0.
  2. Measure the resistance of the CT signal source.
  3. No resistance (open circuit) ⇒ CT is damaged — replace with a new one.
